title: Verb Types (る, う or Irregular?)
description: Learn to tell a verb's type from its dictionary form — the first step for every conjugation.

points.title: Doesn't end in る → う-verb
points.summary: 書く, 話す, 待つ, 死ぬ, 遊ぶ, 読む, 泳ぐ, 買う: always う-verbs.
points.body:
**How to tell the verb type** — look at the dictionary form:

- Doesn't end in る (〜う, 〜く, 〜す, 〜つ …) → **う-verb**, always.
- Ends in る, and the sound before it is **a / u / o** (分**か**る, 作**る**→つく**る**, 乗**る**) → **う-verb**, always.
- Ends in **-iる / -eる** (見る, 起**き**る, 食**べ**る) → usually a **る-verb**.
- …except a short list of common う-verbs: **帰る, 入る, 走る, 切る, 知る, 要る, 限る, 喋る, 滑る, 焦る, 減る, 蹴る, 握る, 散る**.
- **する** and **来る** are irregular; 勉強する and other noun + する verbs conjugate like する.

**Why it matters**
- る-verbs drop る: 食べ**ない**, 食べ**ます**, 食べ**て**.
- う-verbs change the last sound: 帰**ら**ない, 帰**り**ます, 帰**って**.

**Check yourself:** if you know the ない-form, it tells you the type — 帰**ら**ない has an あ-row sound, so 帰る is an う-verb.

points.summary: 見る, 起きる, 食べる, 教える: drop る for every form.

points.summary: 分かる, 作る, 乗る, 取る: the sound before る is not i or e, so it's an う-verb.

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{書|か}く**?
questions.explanation: {書|か}く ends in く, not る. Every verb that doesn't end in る is an う-verb: 書かない, 書きます, 書いて.
notes: Only verbs ending in る can be る-verbs.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{食|た}べる**?
questions.explanation: The sound before る is べ (-e), and -iる / -eる verbs are normally る-verbs: just drop る → 食べない, 食べます, 食べて.
notes: An う-verb would turn る into ら: 食べらない — but it's 食べない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{分|わ}かる**?
questions.explanation: The sound before る is か (-a). Verbs in -aる are always う-verbs: 分からない, 分かります, 分かって.
notes: A る-verb would just drop る: 分かない — but it's 分からない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **する**?
questions.explanation: する is one of only two irregular verbs: しない, します, して.
notes: It doesn't follow the regular pattern: しない, します, して.
It doesn't follow the regular pattern: しない, します, して.

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{来|く}る**?
questions.explanation: 来る is irregular — its vowel changes: 来ない, 来ます, 来て (こない, きます, きて).
notes: It doesn't follow the regular pattern: 来ない, 来ます, 来て.
It doesn't follow the regular pattern: 来ない, 来ます, 来て.

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{勉強|べんきょう}する**?
questions.explanation: {勉強|べんきょう}する is noun + する, so it conjugates exactly like する: 勉強しない, 勉強します, 勉強して.
notes: It doesn't follow the regular pattern: 勉強しない, 勉強します, 勉強して.
